content: The winner of the World Rapid Chess Championship in Riyadh in 2017 was not specified in the provided search results. However, according to Document [5], the current world rapid champion as of 2017 is Indian grandmaster Vishwanathan Anand [5].

The United States currency left the gold standard in 1971, when the U.S. government suspended the convertibility of the U.S. dollar to gold [2]. However, the U.S. officially left the gold standard in 1970 [4]. In a series of laws and executive orders in March and April 1933, the government suspended the gold standard for United States currency [5].
The Svalbard Global Seed Vault was officially opened on 26 February 2008 [2], although the first seeds arrived in January 2008 [2]. The vault was scheduled to open in late 2008 [3].
The national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago, "Forged from the Love of Liberty," was composed by Patrick S. Castagne in 1962 [1][3].

Bourbon Street is a historic street in the French Quarter of New Orleans, famous for its many bars and strip clubs, with 17.74 million visitors in 2017 alone [1]. St. Charles Avenue is a thoroughfare in New Orleans, home to the St. Charles Streetcar Line, and is also famous for the dozens of mansions that adorn the tree-lined boulevard [2].
The singer of the Beatles' song "Do You Want to Know a Secret?" was George Harrison [1]. The song was written by John Lennon but credited to Lennon–McCartney [1].

The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution was ratified by the states on December 6, 1865 [2]. The ratification process was completed after North Carolina and Georgia gave the amendment the final votes needed for it to become part of the Constitution [1]. Secretary of State Seward certified that the Thirteenth Amendment had become valid on December 18, 1865 [1].

The song "Don't Matter to Me" by Drake, featuring posthumous vocals from Michael Jackson, was released as the album's fourth single on July 6, 2018 [1]. It was set to be released to US rhythmic radio on July 10, 2018 alongside "In My Feelings" [1].
England won the FIFA World Cup in 1966, when they hosted the finals and defeated West Germany 4–2 in the final [1][2].

Booker T. Washington delivered his famous Atlanta Exposition Speech, which laid the foundation for the Atlanta compromise, to a predominantly white audience at the Cotton States and International Exposition in Atlanta, Georgia on September 18, 1895 [3]. In the speech, Washington called to the blacks, who composed one third of the Southern population, to join the world of work and declared that the South was where blacks were given their chance [2].
Louisiana adopted a right-to-work law in 1976 [3]. The state was the last traditional southern state to adopt such legislation [2].
The first North American Indigenous Games were held in 1990 in Edmonton, Alberta [1]. The 2017 North American Indigenous Games were held in Toronto, Ontario, Canada from July 16 to 23 [3].
Stephen King's Dark Tower series consists of eight books [1]. The series incorporates themes from multiple genres, including dark fantasy, science fantasy, horror, and Western [1].

The Myrtle Beach SkyWheel, a Ferris wheel in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, is located near Plyler Park [3]. It is the tallest Ferris wheel in the United States east of the Mississippi River, standing at 187 feet [3].

The third season of the animated television series "Rick and Morty" originally aired on Cartoon Network's late night programming block Adult Swim [1]. The season premiered with "The Rickshank Rickdemption" on April 1, 2017, as part of Adult Swim's annual April Fools' prank, and the remaining episodes began airing weekly nearly four months later on July 30, 2017 [1].

The term that refers to linking a currency value to the value of gold is the "gold standard" [1]. Under the gold standard, a country's government declares that it will exchange its currency for a certain weight in gold [2]. A gold standard is a special case of a currency board where the value of the national currency is linked to the value of gold instead of a foreign currency [4].

Football was first introduced in the Olympics at the 1908 Summer Olympics, which was an official FIFA-supervised Olympic competition for amateur players only [5]. The Olympic football competition was initially contested as an IOC-recognised Olympic sport at the 1900 and 1904 Summer Olympics, and at the 1906 Intercalated Games [5]. The first Olympic football competition in which professionals were allowed was the 1984 Summer Olympics [1].

The Cleveland Browns returned to the NFL in 1999, after a three-year period of deactivation [1]. The franchise was considered a continuation of the previous franchise, with its history and colors remaining in Cleveland [3].
St. Petersburg is a city located in Pinellas County, Florida [1]. It is situated on the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa [1].

The first handheld camera was introduced by George Eastman in 1888 with the Kodak camera, which was marketed with the slogan "You press the button, we do the rest" [3]. Thomas Edison developed a portable film camera in 1896 [1]. Polish inventor Kazimierz Prószyński first demonstrated a hand-held film camera in 1898, but it was not reliable [1].

In the 2010 film adaptation of Tim Burton's Alice Through the Looking Glass, Anne Hathaway portrayed the White Queen, renamed "Mirana of Marmoreal" [1]. In the 1987 animated film Alice Through the Looking Glass, Phyllis Diller played the role of the White Queen [4].

The Ordinance of Secession in South Carolina was signed on December 20, 1860 [2]. However, the document outlining the reasons for secession, known as the "Declaration of the Immediate Causes Which Induce and Justify the Secession of South Carolina from the Federal Union," was written by Christopher Memminger [1].

The direct capital costs incurred by the host city and country to host the Rio Olympics were USD 4.6 billion [1]. This figure compares with costs of USD 40–44 billion for Beijing 2008 and USD 51 billion for Sochi 2014, the two most expensive Olympics in history [1].
The festival of Holi marks the end of winter and the beginning of spring [1][2]. It also celebrates the beginning of the new year and is a time to reset and renew relationships [3].

The song "Brown Eyes" was composed and sung by Christine McVie of Fleetwood Mac [1]. Additionally, "Brown Eyes" was co-written by La Toya Jackson and Amir Bayyan, and later recorded by Jimmy Cliff [5].
Josh Martinez won the game in a 5–4 vote against Paul Abrahamian in Big Brother 19 [3].

The United States purchased the Gadsden Purchase from Mexico, with the first draft of the treaty signed on December 30, 1853, by James Gadsden, U.S. ambassador to Mexico, and by Antonio López de Santa Anna, president of Mexico [1]. The U.S. Senate voted in favor of ratifying the treaty with amendments on April 25, 1854 [1].

The Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) was established by Reverend John Flynn on 15 May 1928 in Cloncurry, Queensland [1]. The Australian Inland Mission Aerial Medical Service, which would later become the RFDS, was established by Reverend John Flynn in 1928 [1][2].

The song "Genie in a Bottle" was released on June 22, 1999 [1]. It became the biggest summer song of 1999 and reached number one on the "Billboard" Hot 100, staying there for five consecutive weeks [2].
The second season of the Netflix series Jessica Jones was released on March 8, 2018 [1]. It was released to coincide with International Women's Day [1].

The Romano-Britons expelled the magistrates of the usurper Constantine III, ostensibly in response to his failures to use the Roman garrison he had stripped from Britain to protect the island, around 410 [1]. The Romano-Britons first appealed to Rome and when no help was forthcoming, they expelled the Roman officials and took charge of their own affairs [2].

The torch at the 2012 Olympics was lit by seven young athletes, each nominated by a famous British Olympian, after it was carried into the stadium by Sir Steve Redgrave [1]. Steve Redgrave received the flame from young footballer Jade Bailey, the torchbearer on the boat, and carried it into the Olympic Stadium [2].

The Latin word "camera obscura" means "dark room" [1]. It refers to the natural optical phenomenon where an image of a scene is projected through a small hole and forms an inverted image on a surface opposite to the opening [1].

The Red Sox set a franchise record for the most wins in a season with 105 in 1912 [3]. However, they also set a new franchise record for wins in a season by surpassing the prior mark of 105 in the 2018 season [2].
The winner of Britain's Got Talent in 2015 was Jules O'Dwyer & Matisse, a dog tricks duo [1].

The introduction of cricket to India is attributed to the East India Company [1]. The earliest reference to cricket being played in the Indian sub-continent was in 1721, when British sailors of the East India Company were reported to be playing cricket at Cambay, near Baroda [3]. The Parsi community in Mumbai (formerly Bombay) was the first Indian community to start playing the game, establishing the Oriental Cricket Club in 1848 [4].

In the original Baywatch television series, Matt Brody was played by David Charvet [1]. In the 2017 film Baywatch, Matt Brody was portrayed by Zac Efron [not mentioned in the search results, but known from external sources].

The Black Stallion is an Arabian stallion, as showcased in the film "The Black Stallion" [3] and mentioned in the context of Arabian horses in the article "Arabian horse" [4]. In the novel "The Black Stallion" by Walter Farley, the Black Stallion is known as the Black or Shêtân, an Arab stallion [2].

The most common type of rock in Earth's crust is igneous rock, which makes up about 64.7% of the Earth's crust by volume [1]. Of these, 66% are basalts and gabbros, 16% are granite, and 17% granodiorites and diorites [1].

The song "Fooled Around and Fell in Love" was written and performed by blues guitarist Elvin Bishop, with the lead vocals sung by Mickey Thomas [1]. Elvin Bishop did not sing lead vocals on the track, feeling that his gravelly voice wouldn't do the song justice, and instead invited vocalist Mickey Thomas to sing it [1].
The song "As Time Goes By" was written by Herman Hupfeld in 1931 [1][3].
The systolic blood pressure value is the pressure when the ventricles are contracting, near the end of the cardiac cycle [1]. It is the peak pressure in the arteries [1].

In the context of "That's So Raven," Raven's mother, Cori, was involved with Robin (Dick Grayson), and was married twice, both times to Tamaranean men: once to the Prince Karras to seal a peace treaty; and once to General Phy'zzon out of love [2].

The film "There Will Be Blood" takes place in Southern California during the late 19th and early 20th centuries' oil boom [2]. The story revolves around a silver miner-turned-oilman on a ruthless quest for wealth [2].
The New York Jets lost the first televised Monday Night Football game to the Cleveland Browns, 31–21 [1].
The New England Patriots have won the Super Bowl in a row three times: in 2001, 2003, and 2004 [1], and also in 2014 and 2016 [1].

In networking, Network Address Translation (NAT) is a method of remapping one IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets [1]. This technique was originally used to avoid readdressing every host when a network was moved, and has become a popular tool in conserving global address space in the face of IPv4 address exhaustion [1].

The third movie in the How to Train Your Dragon series, titled "How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World", was originally scheduled for release on June 17, 2016 [3], but the release date was later moved to February 22, 2019 [2].

The song "I'm Not Gonna Miss You" was co-written by Glen Campbell and producer Julian Raymond [1]. It was released on September 30, 2014, for the soundtrack to the documentary "Glen Campbell: I'll Be Me" [1]. The song was nominated for Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards [2].

In the 2000 live-action film "How the Grinch Stole Christmas!", the role of Cindy Lou Who was played by actress Taylor Momsen [1]. In the TV series or film "Carmen Jones", Olga James played the role of Cindy Lou [5].

The ribeye comes from the rib section of a beef animal, specifically from the longissimus dorsi muscle, as well as the complexus and spinalis muscles [1]. In the United States, the term rib eye steak is used for a rib steak with the bone removed [2].

The Lion King debuted on Broadway at the New Amsterdam Theater on October 15, 1997, with the official opening on November 13, 1997 [1]. The Broadway production later moved to the Minskoff Theatre on June 13, 2006 [2].

The Golden State Warriors are an American professional basketball team based in Oakland, California [1]. They compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA), as a member of the league's Western Conference Pacific Division [1]. The team plays its home games at the Oracle Arena [1].
The music for the film How to Train Your Dragon was composed by John Powell [1]. Powell's score earned him his first Academy Award nomination and his third BAFTA nomination [1].

The first rocket to reach space was a German V-2 rocket, on a vertical test flight in June 1944 [1]. However, it was the third V-2 rocket, launched on October 3, 1942, that became the first man-made object to enter space by following its trajectory perfectly and landing 193 km away [2].

Hungry Jack's owns and operates or sub-licenses all of the Burger King/Hungry Jack's restaurants in Australia [2]. The company is responsible for licensing new operators, opening its own stores and performing standards oversight of franchised locations in Australia [2]. Hungry Jack's has over 390 locations across Australia [4].
In the 2000 direct-to-video film "Joseph: King of Dreams", the song "You Know Better Than I" (also known as "Better Than I") is performed by Joseph (David Campbell) [2][3].

The song "If I Were a Boy" was originally written by BC Jean [1]. It was initially recorded by Jean, but her record company rejected it [1]. Jean then reached an agreement with Beyoncé, who recorded her own version of the song for her album "I Am... Sasha Fierce" [1].

The film "10 Things I Hate About You" is a loose modernization of William Shakespeare's comedy "The Taming of the Shrew" and was primarily filmed in the Seattle metropolitan area, with many scenes shot at Stadium High School in Tacoma [1].

In association football, a player can be substituted during a stoppage in play and with the permission of the referee [3]. The player to be substituted must have left the field of play before the substitute can enter [3].

The city in Texas with the highest elevation is El Paso, which has a park, Franklin Mountains State Park, with a peak, North Franklin Mountain, at 7,192 feet [2]. The highest natural point in Texas is Guadalupe Peak, located in Guadalupe Mountains National Park, with an elevation of above sea level [1].
The author of the essay "An Essay on the Principle of Population" was Thomas Robert Malthus [1]. The book was first published anonymously in 1798, but the author was soon identified as Malthus [1].
Bruce Springsteen played at the Super Bowl during Super Bowl XLIII [1]. The Miami Horns played with Springsteen at the halftime show during Super Bowl XLIII [3].
The first season of the TV series Sherlock consisted of three 90-minute episodes [1].

The movie "Summer of '42" was filmed in part at Greenwood, MS, and Vaiden, Mississippi [1]. The film's story is based on the memoirs of screenwriter Herman Raucher, who spent his 1942 summer vacation on Nantucket Island off the coast of Cape Cod [2][3].
The Portuguese referred to the region that is now known as Mumbai as "Bombaim" [1][2][3].
In the TV show Still Game, Winston buys several electric heaters at an outdoor market in Possilpark [1].
The ratio of the wave height to its wave length is called the significant wave height [1]. It is defined traditionally as the mean wave height (trough to crest) of the highest third of the waves [1].
The New York Knicks last won a championship in 1973 [1].
Disneyland Paris encompasses two theme parks [2]. The two theme parks at Disneyland Paris are Disneyland Park and Walt Disney Studios Park [3].
Ragtime music started to become popular in the 1890s [1][2]. By the start of the 20th century, it became widely popular throughout North America [3].
Yuzuru Hanyu became the first male figure skater to win two consecutive gold medals after Dick Button, winning the men's single figure skating competition at the 2018 Winter Olympics [1].

The Ukrainian Army unveiled its new uniforms on August 24, 2016 [1]. In the United States, the Army Combat Uniform patterned in Operational Camouflage Pattern (OCP) first became available to U.S. Army soldiers on July 1, 2015 [2]. By October 1, 2018, all Airmen will be required to own OCP uniforms [2].

The Philadelphia Phillies won the World Series in 1980, defeating the Kansas City Royals in game 6 on October 21, 1980 [1][3]. This was the team's first NL title since 1950 and their second championship in their 126-year history [2].
The role of Ingrid on Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman was initially played by Ashley Jones, and later by Jennifer Youngs [1].

The DNA-directed synthesis of an RNA molecule is called transcription [2]. This process involves the use of DNA as a template for the synthesis of RNA, with RNA polymerase locally opening the double-stranded DNA to facilitate the synthesis [3].
The third season of RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars premiered on January 25, 2018 [2].

In the Netflix series "Orange Is the New Black", Piper Chapman is played by Taylor Schilling [2][3]. The character Piper Chapman is based on Piper Kerman, author of the non-fiction book "", upon which the series is based [2][3].

The first commercially available cellular phone small enough to be easily carried was the Motorola DynaTAC 8000x, which was released in the USA [3]. Martin Cooper, a former general manager for the systems division at Motorola, led a team that produced this phone and made the first phone call from it [3]. The first mobile telephone call from handheld subscriber equipment was made by Martin Cooper on April 3, 1973 [4].

In the film The Sound of Music, the von Trapp family escapes to Switzerland after driving to the border and then making their way on foot across the frontier into Switzerland to safety and freedom [1]. The final scene shows the family hiking on the Obersalzberg near the German town of Berchtesgaden, within sight of Adolf Hitler's Kehlsteinhaus Eagle's Nest retreat [4].
The murderer in the first Broadchurch was Joe Miller, DS Ellie Miller's husband [2].

In the 2016 film Ghostbusters, the mayor is mentioned but not explicitly played by an actor [1]. However, in the original Ghostbusters, the character Mayor Mulligan is played by a character who is exorcised and carried outside by Winston Zeddemore [2].
The song "Wall to Wall" was recorded by American singer Chris Brown for his second studio album, "Exclusive" (2007) [1]. Chris Brown sang "Wall to Wall" [1].
Argentina has won the FIFA World Cup twice, in 1978 and 1986 [1].

The first person to successfully land the 900 on film at a competition was BMX-Rider Mat Hoffman in Canada in 1989 [1]. However, the 900 can also be attributed to Danny Way, who reportedly landed it in 1989, as seen in an early Santa Cruz film [5].

The longest and most expensive trial in US history was the McMartin preschool trial, which lasted seven years and cost $15 million [1]. Another long trial was the "United States v. Anthony Accetturo et al." RICO trial, which was the longest federal trial in history, lasting 21 months [3].
In the show Hannah Montana, Miley Stewart chooses Jake over Jesse [2].
The first foreigner to receive the Bharat Ratna was Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan of Pakistan in 1987 [3].
The movie "It" (2017) is set in the summer of 1989 in Derry, Maine [2]. The film was primarily shot in the Riverdale neighborhood of Toronto, Ontario, as well as in Port Hope and Oshawa, Ontario [1].
The original twins in the TV series Everybody Loves Raymond were Michael and Geoffrey Barone, who were originally named Matthew and Gregory in the pilot [3][5].
The lead singer of the song "Next to Me" by Imagine Dragons is Dan Reynolds [1].

A pioneer in the field of eyewitness research was Hugo Münsterberg, whose book "On the Witness Stand" (1908) demonstrated the fallibility of eyewitness accounts [1]. Gary L. Wells has also made significant contributions to the field, developing Bayesian methods to evaluate eyewitness identification evidence [2]. Judith Daylen has assessed the reliability of eyewitness testimony, concluding that it is often reliable and has merit, along with John C. Yuille in 1986 [3].
The Shema is found in the Torah in Deuteronomy [1]. The Shema is composed of three portions: Deuteronomy , Deuteronomy , and Numbers [2].

Michael Jordan's last year with the Chicago Bulls was the 1997-98 season, during which he announced his second retirement [1]. This marked the end of the Bulls' dynasty that had dominated the NBA throughout the 1990s [1].
The first Krispy Kreme store was located in a rented building on South Main Street in Winston-Salem, North Carolina [1].

In the 1939 film "The Wizard of Oz", the character Tin Woodman stated that he has neither heart nor brain [1]. The song "If I Only Had a Heart" was sung by the Tin Man, with Jack Haley's voice being heard on the soundtrack, although Buddy Ebsen's voice remained on the group vocals of "We're Off To See The Wizard" [2].

The Vietnam Veterans Memorial was dedicated on Veterans Day in 1982 [1]. The construction of the memorial began on March 16, 1982 [2], and was finished in late October 1982 [2]. The memorial was formally dedicated on November 13, 1982 [2].
The film "Places in the Heart" was filmed in Waxahachie, Texas [1].

In Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege, matches last four minutes for casual and three minutes for competitive [2]. The game features a series of short missions that can be played solo, which have no campaign [1].
O'Loughlin Gaels won the 2016 Kilkenny Senior Hurling Championship after defeating Ballyhale Shamrocks 0-19 to 1-12 in the final [1].

A wind controller, which can be used with a keyboard, is played by blowing into it [1]. Additionally, a keyboard-based breath controller is available, which modulates standard keyboards, computers, and other MIDI devices [1].
After the death of Qutub ud din Aibak, his successor was Shams ud-Din Iltutmish [1].

In the 1955-1956 NBA season, the league had eight franchises: the New York Knicks, Boston Celtics, Philadelphia Warriors, Minneapolis Lakers, Rochester Royals, Fort Wayne Pistons, Tri-Cities Blackhawks, and Syracuse Nationals [3].
The older version of Dottie Hinson in the 1992 film "A League of Their Own" was played by Lynn Cartwright [1].

Neil Armstrong received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Nixon [1]. Armstrong and his Apollo 11 crewmates were awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Richard Nixon [3].
The song "(Remember Me) I'm the One Who Loves You" was written and originally sung by Stuart Hamblen [1].
Esther Cleveland was the only child of a president to be born in the White House, born on September 9, 1893 [1].

According to nuclear experiments, it is easier to convert lead into gold than the reverse reaction, which is the one the alchemists had ardently pursued [1]. In fact, in 1980, Glenn Seaborg successfully transmuted several thousand atoms of bismuth into gold at the Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory using nuclear physics [3]. However, this process was far too expensive to enable the routine manufacture of gold [3].

Benjamin "Ben" Stone, a fictional character in the TV drama "Law & Order", played by Michael Moriarty, resigned at the end of season four [1]. His departure from the series stemmed from actor Michael Moriarty's dispute with the network and U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno [2]. Michael Moriarty left the show in 1994, alleging that his departure was a result of his threatening a lawsuit against then-Attorney General Janet Reno [3].

The combined waters of Lake Michigan and Lake Huron are joined through the Straits of Mackinac [1]. This connection is wide and deep, allowing for the free exchange of water between the two sides [2].

Emperor Constantine I decreed that Sunday would be observed as the Roman day of rest in 321 AD [1]. The Council of Laodicea (363–364 AD) outlawed the observance of the Jewish Sabbath (Saturday) and encouraged Christians to work on Saturday and rest on Sunday [1].

The song "Fairytale of New York" was written by Jem Finer and Shane MacGowan [1]. It was originally released as a single on 23 November 1987 and later featured on the Pogues' 1988 album "If I Should Fall from Grace with God" [1].

Dr. Owen Hunt on Grey's Anatomy was portrayed by Kevin McKidd [1]. He was originally introduced as a recurring character in the season premiere, but was later promoted to a series regular in the fourteenth episode of the season "Beat Your Heart Out" [1].

In the Garage Sale Mystery film series, Lori Loughlin plays the lead role of Jennifer Shannon [1]. The series follows the story of antiques dealer Jennifer (Loughlin) who has a knack for finding crimes [1].
The second season of The Seven Deadly Sins anime, also referred to as the "Signs of Holy War" arc, was released on February 17, 2017, and consisted of 24 episodes [1].
In the TV series Star Trek: Enterprise, Admiral Maxwell Forest was played by Vaughn Armstrong [1]. In the TV series Star Trek, Admiral Valdore was played by Brian Thompson [2].
The 2018 FIFA World Cup took place in Russia from 14 June to 15 July 2018 [1].

The American crime drama television series "Lie to Me" originally ran on the Fox network from January 21, 2009 to January 31, 2011 [3][4]. Fox canceled "Lie to Me" after three seasons on May 11, 2011 [1].

The song "What a Beautiful Name" is by Australian praise and worship group Hillsong Worship, written and led by Brooke Ligertwood [1]. It won two Dove Awards for Song of the Year and Worship Song of the Year in 2017 [1], and also won the 2018 Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song [1].

The Blue Lagoon in Iceland is fed by the water output of the nearby geothermal power plant Svartsengi and is renewed every two days [2]. The water's milky blue shade is primarily caused by silicate minerals [3].

The last mainland population of woolly mammoths existed in the Kyttyk Peninsula of Siberia 9,650 years ago [2]. A small population of woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean until 4,000 years ago [2]. The woolly mammoths of eastern Beringia (modern Alaska and Yukon) had died out about 13,300 years ago [1].

The process that releases nitrogen gas into the atmosphere is denitrification, which is an anaerobic process in which microorganisms reduce nitrate (NO) to atmospheric nitrogen gas (N) [1]. This process is also the reverse of nitrification, which transforms ammonia into nitrate [2].
The Vikram Samvat calendar is the official calendar of Nepal [1]. In addition to Nepal, the Vikram Samvat calendar is also recognized in North and East India, and in Gujarat among Hindus [3].
The last person hanged in England was John Robson Walby (alias Gwynne Owen Evans), who was executed on 13 August 1964 [2].
The song "Anything You Can Do I Can Do Better" comes from the 1946 Broadway musical "Annie Get Your Gun" composed by Irving Berlin [1].

The Ottoman Empire conquered the region of Palestine by December 1516, after defeating the Mamluk forces in the Battle of Yaunis Khan on October 28, 1516 [2]. By this time, the Ottoman Empire had already become the new rulers of the Levant, following their victory in the Battle of Marj Dabiq on August 24, 1516 [2].
The clear and present danger test was replaced in 1969 with the "imminent lawless action" test, as seen in the case "Brandenburg v. Ohio" [2][3].
In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Gamora's adopted sister is Nebula, who is played by Karen Gillan [4].

The first literature of the Anglo-Saxons is often considered to be "Cædmon's Hymn", composed in the 7th century [5]. Old English literature, or Anglo-Saxon literature, encompasses the surviving literature written in Old English in Anglo-Saxon England, in the period after the settlement of the Saxons and other Germanic tribes in England (Jutes and the Angles) c. 450, after the withdrawal of the Romans, and "ending soon after the Norman Conquest" in 1066 [1].
The character Charlie on It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia is portrayed by Charlie Day [1].

The gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) is the maximum operating weight/mass of a vehicle as specified by the manufacturer, including the vehicle's chassis, body, engine, engine fluids, fuel, accessories, driver, passengers, and cargo, but excluding that of any trailers [1].
Jason Sudeikis plays the roles of Holt Richter and Terry Kimple on the TV show "The Cleveland Show" [1][2].

The film "The Greatest Showman" was released in the United States on December 20, 2017 [1]. It had a limited IMAX release on February 2, and a sing-along version was released in the United Kingdom on February 23, 2018 [1]. The film's soundtrack was released in full on December 8, 2017 by Atlantic Records [4].
Olympic National Park is located in the State of Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula [1]. The park is nearly surrounded by the Olympic National Forest [2][3].

The main countries that the Allies fought against in World War 2 were Germany, led by Adolf Hitler [3], and Japan, which attacked the US and Britain in December 1941 [1]. The Soviet Union, led by Joseph Stalin, also faced Nazi Germany during the war [4].

The Carolina Panthers play at Bank of America Stadium [1]. The team owns the stadium, making them one of the few teams in the NFL to own the facility they play in [1]. Bank of America Stadium has hosted seven playoff games and has had over 150 consecutive sellouts starting with the 2002 season [4].

The repetition of phrases or sentences with similar structures or meanings is called repetition [1]. In music, repetition is defined as the repetition of a phrase or melody often with variations in key, rhythm, and voice [2].

The Battle of King's Mountain was a victory for the Patriots, who defeated the Loyalist militia commanded by British Major Patrick Ferguson [2]. This decisive victory was a great boost to Patriot morale and broke the Tories of the Carolina back country as a military force [3].

The song "Give Me a Home Among the Gumtrees" was written in 1974 by Wally Johnson and Bob Brown, also known as Captain Rock [1][2]. It was originally performed as a satirical number in their comedy act at the Flying Trapeze Cafe in Fitzroy, Melbourne [1].
The Bay of Pigs Invasion took place in the Bay of Pigs, a small nondescript bay on the Gulf of Cazones [2]. The Bay of Pigs is located on the southern coast of Cuba [1].

Saint Catherine Street in Montreal is 11.2 km long [1]. It crosses the central business district from west to east, beginning at the corner of Claremont Avenue and de Maisonneuve Boulevard in the city of Westmount, traversing the borough of Ville-Marie, and ending on Notre-Dame Street just east of Viau Street in the borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve [2].

In 2015, Brendon McCullum was initially named as the captain of the New Zealand cricket team for the tour of South Africa in June [2]. However, he was later rested for the tour and replaced by Kane Williamson in July [2].

John Nash's treatment for paranoid schizophrenia included antipsychotic medications and insulin shock therapy [1]. He later refused any further medication after 1970 and was never committed to a hospital again [1].

In a covalent bond, electrons are located between atoms, represented as pairs of electrons located between atoms [1]. These electron pairs are shared between atoms to form a bond, allowing each atom to attain a stable electronic configuration with a full outer shell [4][5].

Blair's 16 Million Reserve hot sauce, produced by Blair's Sauces and Snacks, has a Scoville rating of 16 million units [2]. This is the hottest product offered by the company, with Tabasco sauce being significantly less hot at 2,500 to 5,000 Scoville units [5].

In the children's book "Charlotte's Web", the central character Wilbur is a pig who formed a relationship with a barn spider called Charlotte [4]. The character Wilbur is a pig who yearns for companionship in the barnyard and is befriended by a barn spider named Charlotte [3]. Charlotte writes messages praising Wilbur in her web, such as "Some Pig", in order to persuade the farmer to let him live [5].

In the Australian soap opera "Home and Away," Ailsa Piper plays the role of Ruth's mother, however, in the provided search results, the mother's name is not explicitly mentioned, but it is mentioned that Ailsa Piper plays the role of Ruth Wilkinson's mother in the show "Neighbours" [5].

The longest recorded home run in MLB history was reportedly hit by Babe Ruth, estimated at between 575 and 600 feet [3]. Joey Meyer holds the record for the longest home run in professional baseball history at 582 feet, which he hit on June 3, 1987 at Denver's Mile High Stadium [1].
